questions.q: What is the most common cause of a report timing out or running slowly, before any formal Salesforce limit is reached?
options: Using the Matrix format instead of Tabular
An unfiltered or loosely filtered report over a large object
Scheduling the report for off-peak hours
Adding a chart to the report
questions.explain: Without a selective filter, the report engine has to scan every candidate record before it can group or summarize anything. That's the single most common cause of slow or failed reports, well before any hard platform limit is hit.

questions.q: Roughly how many rows does a Salesforce report display in the browser per run?
options: Unlimited — every matching record always renders
Up to 2,000 rows
Exactly 50 rows
It depends only on the user's license type
questions.explain: Reports display up to 2,000 rows in the browser. This protects rendering performance; export or the API is the path to the full underlying data set.

questions.q: Why do hard limits like scheduled report caps and row display caps exist?
options: To discourage admins from building reports
They only apply to Salesforce Classic, not Lightning
To protect shared platform performance for every user in the org, not just the one running the report
They are set per-user and can always be raised in Setup
questions.explain: An org's infrastructure is shared. Unbounded reports or unlimited scheduled jobs could degrade performance for everyone, so Salesforce enforces ceilings to protect the whole org.

questions.q: Why would switching from Tabular to Summary or Matrix format help a large report run faster?
options: Grouped formats only have to render the groups, not every individual row
Summary and Matrix formats skip the filter step entirely
Tabular reports are always capped at fewer rows than Summary reports
There's no performance difference between formats
questions.explain: Once data is grouped, the report only needs to render the groups and their subtotals, rather than every individual record — which is lighter work than a flat row-by-row Tabular list over the same data.

questions.q: A heavy report is needed by the finance team but doesn't need to be current to the minute. What's the best way to reduce its impact on other users?
options: Delete the report and rebuild it from scratch each month
Run it manually during peak business hours so it's always fresh
Schedule it to run during off-peak hours instead of live during business hours
Remove all filters so it captures every possible record
questions.explain: Scheduling a genuinely heavy report for off-peak hours avoids competing for the same shared resources other users are querying during business hours, while still delivering current-enough results.
